Fight club is about support groups. Every thing related to fight club and project mayhem is a reflection or inversion of the support groups like testicle cancer survivors. Jack in many ways is an everyman, he is lost, sleepless and on autopilot. He only finds peace in his support network (his weekly support groups), but when that is disrupted by a woman he creates fight club. His men only support group, where he projects his masculine notions onto the men around him (similarly lost). He becomes and speaks like a support group leader. Ultimately being wrong, because his image of masculinity as destructive was because of social conditioning (essentially he lacked a mentor/father). So when he reflects on that he tries to destroy fight club/project mayhem. He no longer projects his ideal self as unattainable and becomes the man he wants to be.

Fight club is also about construction and destruction, particularly maintenance and decay. His life at the start is pure consumerism, built out of an ikea catalog. He sees no value in anything he owned, just saw them as solutions to "sofa problems". "The mona lisa is falling apart", a line said a couple of times in the book. The mona lisa embodying perfection preserved under glass, like a living inside concrete walls a foot thick. Yet it is decaying, a sign that it's future is slow destruction. Jack finds freedom in the decaying old house, because it is already destroyed. It has no modern comforts. But Jack is able to build a life in that house; farming, repairing, making soap. He creates a community in shit.

Fight club has one perfect scene. And that's the scene with the store clerk. In it the destruction of the status quo for the clerk leads to motivation and purpose that men lack in modern life. Tyler changes a life threatening to destroy it, but really he just removes the glass cage around it.
